title: Posterior cruciate ligament tear: posterior drawer after dashboard-type blow
vignette: A 20-year-old man comes to the hospital with knee pain after he tripped and landed on his right knee during a soccer game. The anterior portion of his tibia impacted directly against the ground, and he has been unable to bear weight since the injury. On physical examination, the patient's knee appears swollen, and there is excessive posterior displacement of the tibia when pressure is applied to his anterior tibia with the knee in the flexed position. An axial MRI cross section of the right knee at the level of the tibial plateau is shown, with structures labeled A-E; the posteriorly located cruciate ligament is labeled D. Which of the following structures is most likely injured in this patient?

clues.text: anterior portion of his tibia impacted directly against the ground
clues.note: A direct blow to the ANTERIOR proximal tibia drives the tibia backward - the classic mechanism of posterior cruciate ligament (PCL) injury (the 'dashboard injury').

clues.text: excessive posterior displacement of the tibia when pressure is applied to his anterior tibia with the knee in the flexed position
clues.note: A positive POSTERIOR drawer test (tibia sags/displaces backward) indicates PCL rupture, which normally prevents posterior tibial translation.

clues.text: the posteriorly located cruciate ligament is labeled D
clues.note: On the axial MRI, the anterior cruciate ligament lies anterior and the PCL lies posterior; the posterior cruciate (label D) is the injured structure.

whatMatters: A direct blow to the anterior tibia (pushing the tibia backward) + a positive POSTERIOR drawer test = posterior cruciate ligament (PCL) tear. The PCL normally resists posterior displacement of the tibia relative to the femur. On the axial MRI it is the posteriorly located cruciate - label D. Answer D.
strategy: Link the mechanism to the test to the anatomy. Force on the ANTERIOR tibia -> tibia driven POSTERIOR -> PCL torn -> positive posterior drawer. On axial MRI at the tibial plateau, the ACL is anterior and the PCL is posterior; pick the posterior cruciate (D). Reject the ACL (anterior; positive anterior drawer/Lachman), menisci (joint-line tenderness with twisting), and the patellar ligament (extensor mechanism).

eliminations.label: Anterior cruciate ligament - anterior drawer, opposite mechanism
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: the ACL, which resists ANTERIOR displacement of the tibia and sits anteriorly on the MRI. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: ACL tears give a positive ANTERIOR drawer/Lachman after a pivot or a posteriorly directed blow, whereas this patient has posterior displacement. ✅ Correct if: positive anterior drawer/Lachman after a non-contact pivot.

eliminations.label: Lateral meniscus - joint-line, not drawer instability
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: crescent-shaped cartilage lining the lateral tibial plateau. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: meniscal tears cause joint-line tenderness and positive provocative tests (McMurray) with twisting, not a positive posterior drawer. ✅ Correct if: locking/clicking with joint-line tenderness.

eliminations.label: Patellar ligament - extensor mechanism, high-riding patella
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: the patellar tendon/ligament connecting the patella to the tibial tuberosity. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: its rupture causes inability to extend the knee and a high-riding patella, not posterior tibial displacement. ✅ Correct if: sudden inability to extend the knee with patella alta.

eliminations.label: Medial meniscus - joint-line tenderness, not drawer
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: the medial semilunar cartilage. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: meniscal injury causes joint-line pain/mechanical symptoms with twisting, not the posterior drawer laxity seen here. ✅ Correct if: medial joint-line tenderness with a positive McMurray.

reasoning: Direct force on the anterior tibia drives the tibia posteriorly
The PCL normally prevents posterior tibial displacement, so it tears
Positive posterior drawer test confirms PCL rupture
On axial MRI the PCL is the posterior cruciate (label D) -> answer D
mechanism: The anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments cross within the knee joint, running from the femur to the tibia. The POSTERIOR cruciate ligament (PCL) originates on the lateral surface of the medial femoral condyle and inserts on the posterior intercondylar tibia; it prevents POSTERIOR displacement of the tibia relative to the femur. A force directed against the ANTERIOR proximal tibia (falling onto a flexed knee, or the classic 'dashboard injury') pushes the tibia backward and tears the PCL, producing a positive POSTERIOR drawer test (with the knee flexed 90 degrees, the tibia sags/displaces posteriorly). By contrast, the ACL lies anteriorly, resists anterior tibial translation, and is tested by the anterior drawer/Lachman. On an axial MRI at the tibial plateau, the ACL is the anterior cruciate and the PCL is the posterior cruciate (here label D). The menisci (cartilage, joint-line symptoms) and patellar ligament (extensor mechanism) are not tested by the drawer maneuvers.

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid MSK > knee ligaments: PCL prevents posterior tibial displacement (posterior drawer, dashboard injury); ACL prevents anterior displacement (anterior drawer/Lachman).

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Anterior-tibia blow -> posterior tibial displacement -> PCL; on axial MRI the posterior cruciate is D.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on posterior/anterior drawer test, cruciate ligaments, tibial plateau, or dashboard injury? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: ACL = anterior drawer/Lachman (opposite); menisci = joint-line/McMurray; patellar ligament = extensor mechanism/patella alta.

difficulty.label: 🖼️ Imaging / diagram
difficulty.text: On the axial knee MRI at the tibial plateau: the anteriorly located cruciate is the ACL; the posteriorly located cruciate (label D) is the PCL. Anchor: 'posterior displacement + posterior cruciate = D.'

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: PCL tear -> posterior drawer, dashboard/anterior-tibia blow; ACL tear -> anterior drawer/Lachman, pivot injury.
